messages:
incident-bot: ALERT fired for synthetic check `synth/canary-prefix/apac1` — 5xx rate 23% over 5m. PagerDuty incident INC-4205 created: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/INC-4205

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification sent to #incidents and on-call. Escalation level: P1 -> oncall team.

jamal: acked. I'm the on-call and taking this. Pulling traces and gateway logs now.

oncall-eu: quick heads-up — seeing matching errors from prober cluster in apac1 around 23:05 UTC. Reproducing: `curl -v https://apac1.redwood-inference/synth-check` shows 502s.

alex: any idea if customers are affected or is this internal synthetic-only?

jamal: early look: about ~0.4% of total requests in the window are affected. Most are canary/synth probes but there are some user-facing API 502s for hosted endpoints. Collecting sample request_ids. Running query:
```
SELECT request_id, model, response_code FROM logs
WHERE region = 'apac1' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes' AND response_code >= 500
LIMIT 20;
```

rachel: I'm seeing the model-host pool in apac1 returning a lot of `503 backend_unavailable` errors and connection resets. CPU and NIC on a subset of nodes spiking. Could be a noisy workload or process oom.

jamal: quick mitigation: shifting synthetic routing away from apac1 to apac2 to reduce fanout and isolate failure. Running reroute: `./infra/runbook reroute-synth --from apac1 --to apac2`

incident-bot: Auto-remediation triggered: `synth-fanout-reduce` script started (timeout 5m). PagerDuty: escalated to Tier2.

maria: I scaled the apac1 dedicated-inference pool by +2 GPUs (prod-dedicated-apac1) and kicked a rolling restart on the three nodes showing NIC errors. Watching metrics now.

jamal: after reroute + scale, 5xx dropped to ~1.5% over the last minute. Error budget looks stable. Metrics: https://metrics.redwood/inference/apac1?m=5xx_rate

rachel: confirmed. Support triage reports no major customer-impacting errors in the last 10m, most visible failures were internal probes and a handful of hosted API retries. Impact classification: LIMITED. :white_check_mark:

alex: great job. Please capture runbook steps and add any logs pointing to root cause (OOM, kernel-level NIC resets?). Anyone pulled dmesg or kernel logs?

jamal: capturing logs now — snippet:
```
Mar 15 23:04:58 host-17 kubelet[1]: OOMKilled process=llm_worker pid=2234
Mar 15 23:05:01 host-17 kernel: eth0 tx timeout, resetting
Mar 15 23:05:03 host-17 systemd: restarting inference-worker.service
```

oncall-eu: I'm going to hand this off to @maria — her shift starts in ~20m and she's up to speed. Maria, please monitor for 30m then decide if PD should stay open.

pagerduty: Incident INC-4205 acknowledged by jamal. Status: active -> monitoring. Auto-resolve window configured: 60 minutes of stable metrics.

jamal: closing active interventions for now. Opening internal incident doc INC-4205-RCA and assigning owners: root cause investigation (rachel), infra follow-up (maria), SRE postmortem (jamal). If errors reappear, escalate immediately to PD level2.

maria: noted. I'll keep an eye on apac1 and post a summary in the incident doc in ~1h.

jamal: thread locked for now — will add more if anything changes. Thanks everyone for quick ops.
